question:
Choose the idiom/phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

Family dispute erupted soon after grandpa’s death as he left **some unclear things** in his will.
solution:
The correct answer is** Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"A grey area"** means something** that is not clearly defined or is open to interpretation. **(अस्पष्ट क्षेत्र)

 
 
• **Example: **The rules regarding the use of company property are*** a grey area.***
 
 
 
• **"A grey area"** refers to an **ambiguous situation,** especially one that is not clear-cut or straightforward. (अस्पष्ट क्षेत्र)
 
 
• **Example: **The law about internet privacy is still **a grey area.**
 
 

Therefore, the correct idiom for the given phrase is "A grey area"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Break a leg** (सफलता की शुभकामनाएं): This is a way to wish someone good luck, especially before a performance.

 
 
• **Example:** Before the play started, everyone told the actors** to break a leg.**
 
 
 
• **Beat around the bush** (इधर-उधर की बात करना): To avoid talking about what is important.
 
 
• **Example:** Stop** beating around the bush** and tell me what you want.
 
 
 
• **Crack a book** (पढ़ाई करना शुरू करना): To open a book to study.
 
 
• **Example:** You need to **crack a book **if you want to pass the exam.
 
 

31:Td53,

The correct answer is **Option 3)**
